__dayInLife: On a cross-functional team, your day centers on the words and brand of the product. You carry out and see through the core content work: shaping brand identity, taking stock of the product's content in a content inventory, and writing the copy that guides people, from headlines down to the small microcopy on a button. Around that, you are pulled into a wide slice of the team's work as an advisor. You sit in on research sessions and design reviews, weigh in on wireframes, information architecture, and prototypes, and help shape strategy, positioning, and go-to-market thinking so the voice stays consistent everywhere. A typical day mixes focused making, drafting and refining content in Figma and FigJam, with collaboration: a standup, a working session with designers or researchers, and quick reviews where your read on clarity and tone helps other people's work land. You share drafts early and rough, expect feedback, and improve in short loops rather than polishing alone.

Academia.gaps: In this role your daily work is shaping brand identity, taking stock of content, and writing copy, and you both carry that work out and see it through to a finished, usable result. It rests on craft like Interaction Design and Information Architecture, and produces pieces like an Editorial Style Guide, Microcopy, and a Content Inventory. Academia set you up for the thinking behind it: Research Facilitation, Research Analysis, and Written Communication all transfer, and turning dense ideas into clear prose is close to good copywriting. What is new is the visual and structural craft, and the tools shift from papers to Figma, Notion, and FigJam. The real adjustment is rhythm, from long solitary study to short loops and shared rough drafts.
Academia.training: Your research and writing are strong, so aim early energy at the craft you will own. Start with Interaction Design and Information Architecture, the least familiar skills. Practice on the real work, drafting a small brand identity or content inventory rather than reading about it. Since you see this work through to done, learn to shape a full Editorial Style Guide, beyond a single paragraph. Pick up Figma and FigJam on a real task, and learn Lean UX for the team pace. Lean on your writing while the visual craft catches up.

Pick up Figma and FigJam on real work. Learn Lean UX for the rhythm. Keep your gift for clear, exact writing; copy depends on it.
